name: Monkeygland steak
summary: Pan-seared rump steak under a dark, sweet-and-tangy sauce of onion, chutney, tomato sauce and Worcestershire, the South African steakhouse classic made at home.
about: Monkeygland sauce is a South African invention with no monkey in it: a thick sauce of fried onion, fruit chutney, tomato sauce and Worcestershire. It is usually traced to Johannesburg's hotel kitchens in the early 20th century and became a fixture of steakhouse menus and family steak nights alike.
steps: Take the steaks out of the fridge 20 minutes before cooking, pat them dry and season both sides with salt and pepper.
Make the sauce: heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a small saucepan over medium heat and fry the onion for 5–6 minutes, until soft and golden. Add the garlic and fry for 30 seconds, until fragrant.

Stir in the tomato sauce, chutney, Worcestershire sauce, vinegar, brown sugar, water and hot sauce, if using. Bring to a simmer, then cook on low for 8–10 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick and glossy. Keep warm.

Heat the remaining oil in a heavy frying pan or griddle over high heat until it just begins to smoke. Sear the steaks for 3–4 minutes a side for medium-rare (firm at the edges, springy in the middle) or 5 minutes a side for medium, turning once.
Spoon a little sauce over each steak in the pan for the last minute so it bubbles and clings, then lift the steaks onto a board and rest for 5 minutes.
Serve the steaks with the rest of the warm sauce poured over, with chips or mash and a green salad.
prepNote: The sauce keeps a week in a jar in the fridge; warm it while the steak cooks.
